description: X5.8. The multimodal aerial manipulator of Wopereis et al., IEEE Robotics & Automation Magazine 2018: a 2.1 kg hexarotor (6 x ESC + ElectricDrive + Propeller, 950 Kv, 10x4.5 in, 16 V, 78 N maximum thrust) with a servo-driven carbon tube (0.23 kg, L_m = 0.6 m), a rubber shock mount (a compliant spherical joint) and a 0.15 kg end-effector on three omnidirectional wheels that roll on a wall at x = 1.6 m. A discrete phase machine switches the PX4-style free-flight cascade, the engage controller and the gain-scheduled LQR contact controller (design/design.py derives K(theta_sp) from the constrained dynamics). The 34 s run starts in hover, approaches in free flight, engages with theta_sp ramping 12 -> 20 deg, holds contact with theta_sp -> 27 deg, climbs 0.30 m and returns by open-loop wheel commands, disengages by C = 0.75 m and hovers. Every number below is a measurement of this model on the real worker (reltol 1e-4); the tolerances are justified in the notes.

checks.note: the run starts in hover: the multirotor centre of mass is at 1 m
rotors start at the hover speed sqrt(m g / (6 kT)) = 534.4 rad/s (2.48 kg, 4.06 N per rotor)
free-flight hover: the total thrust carries the whole system, m g = 2.48 * 9.81 = 24.33 N (measured 24.41 N)
free-flight hover and approach: the multirotor height follows the set-point inside 2 cm (measured 0.9 cm; the static CoM-correction torque and the velocity integrator do the work)
free-flight approach: x follows the minimum-jerk move 0.45 -> 0.75 m inside 5 cm (measured 3.5 cm at the peak speed of the move)
phase 0 (free flight) before the engage request
engage is allowed only within 30 cm: the wheel plane is 0.19 m from the wall when the engage is requested
phase 1 (engage) while the multirotor pushes into the wall
phase 2 (contact) once the wall has stopped the multirotor
phase 3 (disengage) after the request at 28.5 s
engage request at 4.5 s (the 30 cm guard is already satisfied)
the contact phase starts when the wheel plane has been within 2 cm of the wall at rest for 0.3 s (measured 6.12 s; the first wheel touches at 5.07 s)
disengage request at 28.5 s
pitch reference theta_sp = 12.2 deg (0.1 s into the 4 s ramp of 8 deg)
pitch reference theta_sp = 20 deg (end of the 4 s engage ramp)
pitch reference theta_sp = 27 deg (end of the contact ramp)
contact established and kept: the normal force on wheel 1 stays positive through the contact phase (measured minimum 1.55 N)
contact established and kept: the normal force on wheel 2 stays positive through the contact phase (measured minimum 2.29 N)
contact established and kept: the normal force on wheel 3 stays positive through the contact phase (measured minimum 2.24 N)
quasi-static normal force at theta_sp = 20 deg: m g tan(theta_sp) = 2.33 * 9.81 * tan(20 deg) = 8.32 N (measured 8.29 N)

quasi-static normal force at theta_sp = 27 deg: 2.33 * 9.81 * tan(27 deg) = 11.65 N (measured 11.41 N, 2 % low: the pitch settles 0.5 deg short of the reference and the end-effector's weight is carried by the wall)

measured wall force vs the prediction m g tan(theta_sp) while theta_sp ramps and the end-effector climbs: at most 0.85 N (7 %) apart (measured 0.68 N). The formula ignores the 0.38 kg of arm and end-effector and the wheel geometry, as the paper notes
|roll| below the paper's 7.5 deg (0.1309 rad) bound during contact (measured 0.84 deg)
|yaw| below the paper's 7.5 deg bound during contact (measured 0.91 deg)
the pitch follows the reference theta_sp inside 1.5 deg after the ramps (measured 0.84 deg)
the arm follows mu_c = theta_sp = 27 deg = 0.471 rad (0.467 rad measured: the servo droops under the arm and end-effector weight)
end-effector height before the locomotion (it rests on the wall by wheel friction)
end-effector height after 6 s at command 0.125: 0.125 * 0.4 m/s * 6 s = 0.30 m up (measured +0.294 m: the wheels slip a little)
after the 2 s pause and 6 s at -0.125 it is back where it started (travel 2 x 0.30 m; measured -0.305 m)
position independence: the multirotor follows the end-effector up and down inside 1.5 cm with no change of its set-points (measured 0.7 cm)
the end-effector does not drift sideways while climbing: |y| below 3 cm (measured 1.5 cm, constant)
the controller set-points are untouched in contact: the position set-point z is constant from 8 s to 28 s
disengage: the multirotor ends at x_b(t_d) - C = 0.9412 - 0.75 = 0.1912 m (the latched set-point is 0.1943 m; measured 0.1872 m)
disengage: the wheel plane is C = 0.75 m from the wall (measured 0.7497 m)
stable hover after the disengage: speed below 5 cm/s over the last second (measured 1.9 cm/s)
stable hover after the disengage: |pitch| below 1 deg over the last second (measured 0.5 deg)
rotor speed stays below the 957 rad/s of the 13 N (78 N total) limit (measured peak 729 rad/s)
the servo stays below its 8.4 N m stall torque (measured 4.4 N m)

scenes/aerial-contact.sdf resolves against the run; the arm tip (0.6, 0, 0) of the link arm_link follows the pose chain of the model, which proves the sign of the arm joint axis; 3 mm tolerance for the compliant held rotations of the servo joint (kr = 500 N m/rad under the 1.6 N m arm weight moment)
no solver, structure or unit warnings and no event-limit W206: all storage elements are integral and the 4 ms ticks never chatter
